claim: Pathogenic mycobacteria pose a sustained threat to global human health.
source: Pathogenic mycobacteria pose a sustained threat to global human health.
evidence: This is a general statement about the public health impact of pathogenic mycobacteria, supported by established scientific knowledge and consensus.

claim: Cytochrome bcc complexes have gained interest as targets for antibiotic drug development.
source: Recently, cytochrome bcc complexes have gained interest as targets for antibiotic drug development.
evidence: This statement reflects current research trends and is supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: There is currently no structural information for the cytochrome bcc complex from pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: However, there is currently no structural information for the cytochrome bcc complex from these pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study, based on literature review.

claim: The structure of M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc alone was determined at 2.68 Å resolution by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
source: Here, we report the structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome bcc alone (2.68 Å resolution) and in complex with clinical drug candidates Q203 (2.67 Å resolution) and TB47 (2.93 Å resolution) determined by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The structure of M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc in complex with Q203 was determined at 2.67 Å resolution by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
source: Here, we report the structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome bcc alone (2.68 Å resolution) and in complex with clinical drug candidates Q203 (2.67 Å resolution) and TB47 (2.93 Å resolution) determined by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The structure of M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc in complex with TB47 was determined at 2.93 Å resolution by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
source: Here, we report the structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome bcc alone (2.68 Å resolution) and in complex with clinical drug candidates Q203 (2.67 Å resolution) and TB47 (2.93 Å resolution) determined by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc forms a dimeric assembly.
source: M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc forms a dimeric assembly with endogenous menaquinone/menaquinol bound at the quinone/quinol-binding pockets.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Endogenous menaquinone/menaquinol is bound at the quinone/quinol-binding pockets in M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc.
source: M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc forms a dimeric assembly with endogenous menaquinone/menaquinol bound at the quinone/quinol-binding pockets.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Q203 is bound at the quinol-binding site in M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc.
source: We observe Q203 and TB47 bound at the quinol-binding site and stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314, residues that are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: TB47 is bound at the quinol-binding site in M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc.
source: We observe Q203 and TB47 bound at the quinol-binding site and stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314, residues that are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Q203 is stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314.
source: We observe Q203 and TB47 bound at the quinol-binding site and stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314, residues that are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: TB47 is stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314.
source: We observe Q203 and TB47 bound at the quinol-binding site and stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314, residues that are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314 are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: We observe Q203 and TB47 bound at the quinol-binding site and stabilized by hydrogen bonds with the side chains of QcrBThr313 and QcrBGlu314, residues that are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in the manuscript.

claim: Approximately 200 species of mycobacteria have been identified.
source: Approximately 200 species of mycobacteria have been identified that have diverse lifestyles, morphologies, and metabolic pathways (Tortoli et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tortoli et al., 2017.

claim: Mycobacteria have diverse lifestyles, morphologies, and metabolic pathways.
source: Approximately 200 species of mycobacteria have been identified that have diverse lifestyles, morphologies, and metabolic pathways (Tortoli et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tortoli et al., 2017.

claim: Mycobacteria belong to the phylum Actinobacteria.
source: Mycobacteria, which belong to the phylum Actinobacteria, have coevolved with humans over thousands of years (Chisholm et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chisholm et al., 2016.

claim: Mycobacteria have coevolved with humans over thousands of years.
source: Mycobacteria, which belong to the phylum Actinobacteria, have coevolved with humans over thousands of years (Chisholm et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chisholm et al., 2016.

claim: Tuberculosis caused by M. tuberculosis leads to approximately 1.2 million fatalities per year.
source: Of these, tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis), is the most serious, leading to ~1.2 million fatalities per year (World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to World Health Organization, 2019.

claim: Infections involving Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium complex are on the rise.
source: Infections involving other pathogenic mycobacteria, for example, Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium complex, are on the rise with some outnumbering those caused by M. tuberculosis in countries including the United States (Donohue, 2018; Johansen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Donohue, 2018 and Johansen et al., 2020.

claim: Some mycobacterial infections outnumber those caused by M. tuberculosis in countries including the United States.
source: Infections involving other pathogenic mycobacteria, for example, Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium complex, are on the rise with some outnumbering those caused by M. tuberculosis in countries including the United States (Donohue, 2018; Johansen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Donohue, 2018 and Johansen et al., 2020.

claim: Mycobacterial infections are difficult to treat due to intrinsic or emerging resistance to many common antibiotics.
source: These infections are notoriously difficult to treat due to intrinsic or emerging resistance to many common antibiotics, thus exacerbating the challenge to find suitable drug targets.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about antibiotic resistance in mycobacteria.

claim: Oxidative phosphorylation has gained interest as a target space for antibiotic drug development.
source: Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) has gained interest as a target space for antibiotic drug development (Cook et al., 2017; Hards et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cook et al., 2017 and Hards et al., 2020.

claim: The protein complexes of the electron transport chain establish a proton motive force across a biomembrane that drives the synthesis of ATP by ATP synthase.
source: In OXPHOS, the protein complexes of the electron transport chain (ETC) establish a proton motive force (PMF) across a biomembrane that drives the synthesis of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) by ATP synthase (Mitchell, 1961).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mitchell, 1961, and represents established knowledge about OXPHOS.

claim: Maintenance of PMF and ATP homeostasis is required for the survival of both replicative and non-replicative mycobacteria.
source: Maintenance of PMF and ATP homeostasis is required for the survival of both replicative and non-replicative (often referred to as dormant) mycobacteria, and its dissipation leads to a rapid loss of cell viability and cell death (Koul et al., 2008; Rao et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Koul et al., 2008 and Rao et al., 2008.

claim: Dissipation of PMF and ATP homeostasis leads to a rapid loss of cell viability and cell death in mycobacteria.
source: Maintenance of PMF and ATP homeostasis is required for the survival of both replicative and non-replicative (often referred to as dormant) mycobacteria, and its dissipation leads to a rapid loss of cell viability and cell death (Koul et al., 2008; Rao et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Koul et al., 2008 and Rao et al., 2008.

claim: The mycobacterial proton-pumping cytochrome bcc-aa3 supercomplex consists of a bcc menaquinol reductase (complex III) and an aa3 oxidase (complex IV) that are tightly associated.
source: The reliance on the PMF and ATP homeostasis thus highlights the importance of the mycobacterial proton-pumping cytochrome bcc-aa3 supercomplex, which consists of a bcc menaquinol reductase (complex III, CIII) and an aa3 oxidase (complex IV, CIV) that are tightly associated (Gong et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2015; Megehee et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gong et al., 2018, Kim et al., 2015, and Megehee et al., 2006.

claim: Several studies support the attractiveness of cytochrome bcc-aa3 for mycobacterial drug development.
source: Several studies support the attractiveness of cytochrome bcc-aa3 for mycobacterial drug development (de Jager et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2019; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Broad-spectrum activity of a therapeutic within the pathogenic mycobacteria is likely given the strict sequence conservation of cytochrome bcc-aa3.
source: Given the strict sequence conservation of this complex (Figure 1), broad-spectrum activity of a therapeutic within the pathogenic mycobacteria is likely (Lee et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020b and reference to Figure 1.

claim: All the cytochrome bcc-aa3 inhibitors published to date appear to target the QcrB subunit of the cytochrome bcc complex.
source: Interestingly, all the cytochrome bcc-aa3 inhibitors published to date appear to target the QcrB subunit (Figure 1) of the cytochrome bcc complex and are likely bound to the menaquinol-binding (Qp) site of the QcrB subunit (Lee et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020b and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Cytochrome bcc-aa3 inhibitors are likely bound to the menaquinol-binding (Qp) site of the QcrB subunit.
source: Interestingly, all the cytochrome bcc-aa3 inhibitors published to date appear to target the QcrB subunit (Figure 1) of the cytochrome bcc complex and are likely bound to the menaquinol-binding (Qp) site of the QcrB subunit (Lee et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020b and inference from the data.

claim: Q203 has been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis.
source: The most advanced of these are Q203 and TB47, which have been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis (de Jager et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013) and Mycobacterium ulcerans (Liu et al., 2019; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Jager et al., 2020, Lu et al., 2019, and Pethe et al., 2013.

claim: TB47 has been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis.
source: The most advanced of these are Q203 and TB47, which have been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis (de Jager et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013) and Mycobacterium ulcerans (Liu et al., 2019; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Jager et al., 2020, Lu et al., 2019, and Pethe et al., 2013.

claim: Q203 has been shown to clear infections due to Mycobacterium ulcerans.
source: The most advanced of these are Q203 and TB47, which have been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis (de Jager et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013) and Mycobacterium ulcerans (Liu et al., 2019; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019 and Scherr et al., 2018.

claim: TB47 has been shown to clear infections due to Mycobacterium ulcerans.
source: The most advanced of these are Q203 and TB47, which have been shown to clear infections due to M. tuberculosis (de Jager et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013) and Mycobacterium ulcerans (Liu et al., 2019; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019 and Scherr et al., 2018.

claim: Q203 has recently completed phase II clinical trials for TB treatment.
source: Q203 has recently completed phase II clinical trials for TB treatment (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03563599; de Jager et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to de Jager et al., 2020 and a clinical trial identifier.

claim: The hybrid supercomplex consisting of M. tuberculosis CIII and M. smegmatis CIV can be stabilized as a functional assembly.
source: Considering that the hybrid supercomplex consisting of M. tuberculosis CIII and Mycobacterium smegmatis CIV can be stabilized as a functional assembly (Kim et al., 2015), we first chose to express and purify this complex to a high level of homogeneity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2015 and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The hybrid supercomplex was confirmed to be active with a turnover number of 23.3 ± 2.4 e-s–1.
source: We confirmed this complex to be active with a turnover number of 23.3 ± 2.4 e-s–1 (mean ± SD, n = 4), in agreement with the previous study that shows M. tuberculosis CIII can functionally complement native M. smegmatis CIII and maintain the growth of M. smegmatis (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from activity assays.

claim: M. tuberculosis CIII can functionally complement native M. smegmatis CIII and maintain the growth of M. smegmatis.
source: We confirmed this complex to be active with a turnover number of 23.3 ± 2.4 e-s–1 (mean ± SD, n = 4), in agreement with the previous study that shows M. tuberculosis CIII can functionally complement native M. smegmatis CIII and maintain the growth of M. smegmatis (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2015.

claim: The structure of the hybrid supercomplex was determined by cryo-EM to an overall resolution of 2.68 Å.
source: The structure of this hybrid supercomplex was determined by cryo-EM to an overall resolution of 2.68 Å, allowing that the components to be clearly assigned in the density map (Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The hybrid supercomplex including the M. tuberculosis CIII dimer forms a pseudo twofold symmetrical compact rod with a slight curvature in the membrane plane.
source: The hybrid supercomplex including the M. tuberculosis CIII dimer forms a pseudo twofold symmetrical compact rod, but with a slight curvature in the membrane plane, as previously observed in the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex (Gong et al., 2018; Wiseman et al., 2018; Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data, supported by citations to Gong et al., 2018 and Wiseman et al., 2018.

claim: The hybrid supercomplex is structurally similar to the supercomplex isolated from M. smegmatis.
source: The hybrid supercomplex is structurally similar to the supercomplex isolated from M. smegmatis (Gong et al., 2018; Wiseman et al., 2018; Figure 2—figure supplement 4), except that subunits LpqE and Unk (probably MSMEG_0987) (Wiseman et al., 2018) were not observed here.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and citations to Gong et al., 2018 and Wiseman et al., 2018.

claim: Subunits LpqE and Unk were not observed in the hybrid supercomplex structure.
source: The hybrid supercomplex is structurally similar to the supercomplex isolated from M. smegmatis (Gong et al., 2018; Wiseman et al., 2018; Figure 2—figure supplement 4), except that subunits LpqE and Unk (probably MSMEG_0987) (Wiseman et al., 2018) were not observed here.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The absence of LpqE and Unk may be due to their depletion during purification or their map density signal was averaged to background noise during structural determination.
source: The absence of these two subunits may be due to their depletion during purification of the supercomplex or their map density signal was averaged to background noise during structural determination.
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for missing subunits.

claim: The topology of M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc and M. smegmatis CIV in the hybrid supercomplex is similar to that of the equivalent subunits in the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex.
source: As expected, the topology of M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc and M. smegmatis CIV in the hybrid supercomplex is also similar to that of the equivalent subunits in the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—figure supplements 4 and 5).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: There are no notable non-native contacts that resulted from the hybrid assembly in the hybrid supercomplex.
source: As such, there is no notable non-native contacts that resulted from the hybrid assembly in the hybrid supercomplex.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The lack of non-native contacts is attributable to the high structural similarity between M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc and M. smegmatis cytochrome bcc.
source: This is attributable to the high structural similarity between the M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc and M. smegmatis cytochrome bcc.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison.

claim: In M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc, QcrA has three transmembrane helices and has a 'U'-shaped structure.
source: In M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc, QcrA has three transmembrane helices (TMHs) and has a 'U'-shaped structure (Figures 2D and 3A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The N-terminal region of QcrA with TMH1/2 and the TMH3 make up the two arms of the 'U' structure.
source: The N-terminal region with TMH1/2 and the TMH3 make up the two arms of the 'U' structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The arms of the QcrA 'U' structure are linked by the region located near the cytoplasmic side.
source: These arms are linked by the region located near the cytoplasmic side.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Attached to QcrATMH3 is the C-terminal domain, which faces the periplasmic side of the membrane and holds the [2Fe-2S] cluster in place.
source: Attached to QcrATMH3 is the C-terminal domain, which faces the periplasmic side of the membrane and holds the [2Fe-2S] cluster in place.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: QcrB has eight transmembrane helices.
source: QcrB has eight TMHs (Figures 2D and 3B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Four transmembrane helices of QcrB are responsible for burying two functionally important heme b cofactors (high potential heme bH and low potential heme bL).
source: Four of these are responsible for burying two functionally important heme b cofactors (high potential heme bH and low potential heme bL).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Heme bL is located between TMH I/II and is near the periplasmic side.
source: Heme bL and heme bH are located between TMH I/II and TMH III/IV, respectively. Heme bL is near the periplasmic side and heme bH near the cytoplasmic side.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Heme bH is located between TMH III/IV and is near the cytoplasmic side.
source: Heme bL and heme bH are located between TMH I/II and TMH III/IV, respectively. Heme bL is near the periplasmic side and heme bH near the cytoplasmic side.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: QcrC is a transmembrane protein with a C-terminal TMH located between QcrBTMH5 and QcrBTMH7.
source: QcrC is a transmembrane protein with a C-terminal TMH located between QcrBTMH5 and QcrBTMH7 (Figures 2D and 3C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The N-terminal periplasmic portion of QcrC can be divided into two heme-containing cytochrome c domains designated D1 and D2.
source: The N-terminal periplasmic portion of QcrC can be divided into two heme-containing cytochrome c domains designated D1 and D2.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The D1 domain of QcrC protrudes out of the core of CIII.
source: The D1 domain protrudes out of the core of CIII, whereas the D2 domain interacts extensively with QcrA and QcrB.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The D2 domain of QcrC interacts extensively with QcrA and QcrB.
source: The D1 domain protrudes out of the core of CIII, whereas the D2 domain interacts extensively with QcrA and QcrB.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: In the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex, the cytochrome cc head domain of QcrC adopts an 'open' or a 'closed' conformation.
source: In the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex, the cytochrome cc head domain of QcrC adopts an 'open' or a 'closed' conformation (Gong et al., 2018; Wiseman et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gong et al., 2018 and Wiseman et al., 2018.

claim: In the hybrid supercomplex structure, the cytochrome cc head domain of QcrC is only in the closed conformation.
source: However, in this structure it is only the closed conformation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The mechanism of action of the hybrid supercomplex including M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc is expected to be the same as that for the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex.
source: Considering the high topology similarity of the subunits and the arrangement of prosthetic groups compared to previous M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex, the mechanism of action of the hybrid supercomplex including M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc is expected to be the same as that for the M. smegmatis CIII2CIV2 supercomplex (Gong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural similarity and supported by a citation to Gong et al., 2018.

claim: Two canonical quinone-binding sites are identified in the M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc structure: the quinol oxidation site (QP site) and the quinone reduction site (QN site).
source: In the present structure, two canonical quinone-binding sites are identified (Figure 3D and E): (i) the quinol oxidation site (QP site) and (ii) the quinone reduction site (QN site).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Other quinone-binding sites with quinone bound are identified remote from the canonical quinone-binding sites and into the membrane space.
source: In addition, other quinone-binding sites with quinone bound are also identified as observed in our previous study (Gong et al., 2018; Figure 3—figure supplement 1). These quinones are remote from the canonical quinone-binding sites and into the membrane space, suggesting that they have a structural rather than functional role.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data, supported by a citation to Gong et al., 2018.

claim: Quinones remote from the canonical quinone-binding sites have a structural rather than functional role.
source: These quinones are remote from the canonical quinone-binding sites and into the membrane space, suggesting that they have a structural rather than functional role.
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of the quinones.

claim: The QP site responsible for menaquinol oxidation is near heme bL.
source: The QP site responsible for menaquinol (MKH2) oxidation is near heme bL, whereas the QN site responsible for MK reduction is close to heme bH (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The QN site responsible for MK reduction is close to heme bH.
source: The QP site responsible for menaquinol (MKH2) oxidation is near heme bL, whereas the QN site responsible for MK reduction is close to heme bH (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: One MK molecule was identified at the QP site with its naphthoquinone ring surrounded by hydrophobic residues QcrBPhe158, QcrBTyr161, QcrBLeu180, QcrBIle183, QcrBMet310, and QcrBMet342.
source: One MK molecule was identified at this site with its naphthoquinone ring surrounded by hydrophobic residues, QcrBPhe158, QcrBTyr161, QcrBLeu180, QcrBIle183, QcrBMet310, and QcrBMet342.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The hydrophobic tail of MK at the QP site wraps around QcrBTMH6 down to its cytoplasmic end and interacts with QcrBMet187, QcrBAla339, QcrBLeu344, and QcrBVal347.
source: Its hydrophobic tail, which contains multiple isoprenoid groups, wraps around QcrBTMH6 down to its cytoplasmic end and in so doing interacts with QcrBMet187, QcrBAla339, QcrBLeu344, and QcrBVal347.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The edge-to-edge distance from MK to heme bL is 15 Å, exceeding the 14 Å limit for efficient physiological electron transfer.
source: The edge-to-edge distance from MK to heme bL is 15 Å, exceeding the 14 Å limit for efficient physiological electron transfer (Page et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data, with the 14 Å limit supported by a citation to Page et al., 1999.

claim: There are no observed hydrogen bonds to the carbonyl groups of MK at the QP site.
source: Furthermore, there are no observed hydrogen bonds to the carbonyl groups of MK, which are needed to help deprotonate MKH2.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Hydrogen bonds to the carbonyl groups of MK are needed to help deprotonate MKH2.
source: Furthermore, there are no observed hydrogen bonds to the carbonyl groups of MK, which are needed to help deprotonate MKH2.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about quinol oxidation mechanisms.

claim: Structural superposition with the inhibitor-bound bc1 complex shows that MK binds deeper into the QP pocket in the bc1 complex than in the currently described complex.
source: In addition, structural superposition with the inhibitor-bound bc1 complex also shows that the MK binds deeper into the QP pocket in the bc1 complex (Birth et al., 2014; Solmaz and Hunte, 2008) than in the currently described complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and citations to Birth et al., 2014 and Solmaz and Hunte, 2008.

claim: The endogenous electron donor MKH2 should bind deeper inside the QP pocket and close to polar residues such as QcrBTyr161, QcrBThr313, and QcrBAsp314 to facilitate electron transfer.
source: Hence, the endogenous electron donor MKH2 should bind deeper inside the pocket and close to polar residues such as QcrBTyr161, QcrBThr313, and QcrBAsp314 (Figure 3D) to facilitate electron transfer.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations and knowledge of electron transfer requirements.

claim: What is observed at the QP site is the oxidized product as it leaves the QP site.
source: Thus, we speculate that what is observed here is the oxidized product as it leaves the QP site.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural observations.

claim: All reported inhibitors including Q203 and TB47 are suggested to interact with the QP site.
source: It is worth noting that all the reported inhibitors including Q203 (Pethe et al., 2013) and TB47 (Lu et al., 2019) are suggested to interact with this QP site.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pethe et al., 2013 and Lu et al., 2019.

claim: The QN site is formed largely by QcrBTMH1, QcrBTMH4, QcrBTMH5 and one loop region of QcrB.
source: In addition, the QN site is formed largely by QcrBTMH1, QcrBTMH4, QcrBTMH5 and one loop region of QcrB (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The head group of MK at the QN site is bound in the pocket interacting with QcrBPhe39, QcrBGlu49, QcrBLeu225, QcrBLeu232, QcrBTrp236, and QcrBPhe262.
source: The head group of MK is bound in this pocket interacting with QcrBPhe39, QcrBGlu49, QcrBLeu225, QcrBLeu232, QcrBTrp236, and QcrBPhe262, and its long hydrophobic tail extends along QcrBTMH1 towards the periplasmic side.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The long hydrophobic tail of MK at the QN site extends along QcrBTMH1 towards the periplasmic side.
source: The head group of MK is bound in this pocket interacting with QcrBPhe39, QcrBGlu49, QcrBLeu225, QcrBLeu232, QcrBTrp236, and QcrBPhe262, and its long hydrophobic tail extends along QcrBTMH1 towards the periplasmic side.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: MK/MKH2 are part of the Q-cycle hypothesis and essential for electron transfer in the cytochrome bcc complex.
source: MK/MKH2 are part of the Q-cycle hypothesis and essential for electron transfer in the cytochrome bcc complex (Gong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gong et al., 2018 and represents established knowledge.

claim: The structure of the hybrid supercomplex in the presence of Q203 was determined by cryo-EM to an overall resolution of 2.67 Å.
source: To obtain atomic information on the mode of binding of Q203 to cytochrome bcc, we have determined the structure of the hybrid supercomplex as described above in the presence of Q203 by cryo-EM to an overall resolution of 2.67 Å (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: Close to the Qp-binding pocket within the membrane of each QcrB of cytochrome bcc there is density for Q203.
source: We observe that close to the Qp-binding pocket within the membrane of each QcrB of cytochrome bcc there is density for Q203 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: All of the Q203 molecules fill each QcrB subunit binding deeply into the QP pocket with identical binding modes.
source: All of the Q203 molecules fill each QcrB subunit binding deeply into the QP pocket and with identical binding modes.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: A hydrogen bond exists between the hydroxyl oxygen of the side chain of QcrBThr313 and the amine in the carboxamide linker of Q203 (3.0 Å).
source: The key interactions that anchor Q203 are (i) a hydrogen bond between the hydroxyl oxygen of the side chain of QcrBThr313 and the amine in the carboxamide linker of Q203 (3.0 Å), (ii) a halogen bond between the chlorine atom of the heterocyclic group and an ordered water molecule that simultaneously forms a hydrogen bond with the hydroxyl oxygen of the side chain of QcrBTyr164 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), (iii) a hydrogen bond between the side chain of QcrBGlu314 and the nitrogen atom in the imidazopyridine ring (3.0 Å), and (iv) a hydrogen bond between the side chain of QcrAHis375 and the nitrogen atom in the imidazopyridine ring (2.98 Å) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The carbon atoms of Q203 make hydrophobic interactions with QcrBGly175, QcrBAla179, QcrBLeu180, QcrBThr184, QcrBSer304, QcrBPro306, QcrBMet310, QcrBAla317, and QcrBMet342.
source: In addition, the carbon atoms of Q203 make hydrophobic interactions with QcrBGly175, QcrBAla179, QcrBLeu180, QcrBThr184, QcrBSer304, QcrBPro306, QcrBMet310, QcrBAla317, and QcrBMet342.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The activity of the supercomplex is inhibited by Q203 in vitro according to the DMNQH2/oxygen oxidoreductase activity assay.
source: These extensive interactions are in agreement with the fact that the activity of the supercomplex is inhibited by Q203 in vitro according to the DMNQH2/oxygen oxidoreductase activity assay.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from activity assays.

claim: After addition of Q203, the turnover number of the hybrid supercomplex reduces to 5.8 ± 2.4 e-s–1 from 23.3 ± 2.4 e-s–1.
source: After addition of Q203, the turnover number of the hybrid supercomplex reduces to 5.8 ± 2.4 e-s–1 from 23.3 ± 2.4 e-s–1 (mean ± SD, n = 4; Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from activity assays.

claim: Functional studies have shown that substitution of QcrBThr313 to alanine confers Q203 resistance.
source: In addition, functional studies have shown that substitution of QcrBThr313 to alanine confers Q203 resistance (Pethe et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pethe et al., 2013.

claim: The binding of Q203 involves residues from both QcrA and QcrB.
source: The binding of Q203 involves residues from both QcrA and QcrB.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Due to the need to form stabilizing interactions between subunits, resistance to Q203 may be more difficult to achieve than if the binding site is within only one subunit.
source: Due to the need to form stabilizing interactions between subunits, resistance may be more difficult to achieve here than if the binding site is within only one subunit.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation of inter-subunit binding.

claim: Reported mutations in Q203-resistant M. tuberculosis are positioned directly where Q203 binds in the structure.
source: Consistently, the mapping of reported mutations in Q203-resistant M. tuberculosis reveals that they are positioned directly where Q203 binds in this structure (Lupien et al., 2020; Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lupien et al., 2020 and structural mapping.

claim: The 2.93 Å cryo-EM map shows density for TB47 and confirms that it binds in the same location as Q203.
source: The 2.93 Å cryo-EM map shows density for TB47 and confirms that it binds in the same location as Q203 (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2, Table 3).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Three hydrogen bond interactions are observed involving the side chains of QcrBThr313, QcrBGlu314, and QcrAHis375 when TB47 binds.
source: Three hydrogen bond interactions are observed involving the side chains of QcrBThr313, QcrBGlu314, and QcrAHis375. Similar interactions are also observed when Q203 binds (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: QcrBTyr161, QcrBLeu171, QcrBGly175, QcrBAla179, QcrBLeu180, QcrBThr184, QcrBMet187, QcrBLeu194, QcrBSer304, QcrBGly305, and QcrBMet342 contribute to TB47 binding, largely through hydrophobic interactions.
source: QcrBTyr161, QcrBLeu171, QcrBGly175, QcrBAla179, QcrBLeu180, QcrBThr184, QcrBMet187, QcrBLeu194, QcrBSer304, QcrBGly305, and QcrBMet342 also contribute to TB47 binding, largely through hydrophobic interactions (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Unlike when Q203 binds, there is no interaction between QcrBTyr164 and TB47.
source: Unlike when Q203 binds (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), there is no interaction between QcrBTyr164 and TB47 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: After addition of TB47, the turnover number for the hybrid supercomplex reduced to 5.1 ± 2.9 e-s–1.
source: However, after addition of TB47, the values of turnover number for the hybrid supercomplex reduced to 5.1 ± 2.9 e-s–1 (mean ± SD, n = 4; Figure 5—figure supplement 4), a similar value that was observed when Q203 binds.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from activity assays.

claim: The absence of interaction between QcrBTyr164 and TB47 does not greatly diminish inhibition.
source: Thus, the absence of this does not greatly diminish inhibition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar inhibition levels observed for Q203 and TB47.

claim: A mutation in TB47-resistant M. smegmatis (M. tuberculosis: H195Y) is close to the Qp-binding site.
source: A mutation in TB47-resistant M. smegmatis (M. tuberculosis: H195Y) is close to the Qp-binding site (Lu et al., 2019; Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lu et al., 2019 and structural mapping.

claim: The H195Y mutation would contribute to steric interference with the binding of TB47, thus accounting for the observed resistance.
source: As a result of the change in shape, it would appear to contribute to steric interference with the binding of TB47, thus accounting for the observed resistance.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis of the mutation.

claim: The structure of apo cytochrome bcc is almost identical with the Q203-bound structure (rmsd of 0.50 Å for all Ca atoms).
source: The structure of apo cytochrome bcc is almost identical with the Q203-bound structure (rmsd of 0.50 Å for all Ca atoms), which suggests that Q203 binding does not significantly affect the overall architecture of cytochrome bcc.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: Q203 binding does not significantly affect the overall architecture of cytochrome bcc.
source: The structure of apo cytochrome bcc is almost identical with the Q203-bound structure (rmsd of 0.50 Å for all Ca atoms), which suggests that Q203 binding does not significantly affect the overall architecture of cytochrome bcc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the small RMSD value.

claim: Residues involved in the binding pocket move outward to adapt to the shape of Q203.
source: A comparison of the Q203-bound and Q203-free cytochrome bcc structures shows residues involved in the binding pocket move outward, thus adapting to the shape of Q203 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing the apo and Q203-bound structures.

claim: The side chains of QcrBSer304, QcrBGlu313, QcrBGlu314, and QcrBMet342 undergo significant conformational changes to form hydrogen bonds with Q203.
source: Specifically, the side chains of QcrBSer304, QcrBGlu313, QcrBGlu314, and QcrBMet342 undergo significant conformational changes to form hydrogen bonds with Q203.
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing the apo and Q203-bound structures.

claim: The binding of TB47 to M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc induces very similar conformational changes in the Qp-binding pocket to those seen for Q203 (rmsd of 0.454 Å for all Ca atoms).
source: The binding of TB47 to M. tuberculosis cytochrome bcc also induces very similar conformational changes in the Qp-binding pocket to those seen for Q203 (rmsd of 0.454 Å for all Ca atoms) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: Q203 and TB47 act competitively with the quinol binding as they almost completely occupy the Qp pocket.
source: When analyzing the superimposed structures (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), it is apparent that Q203 and TB47 act competitively with the quinol binding as they almost completely occupy the Qp pocket.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: Q203 and TB47 are bona fide analogs of the substrate and function by hindering the downstream synthesis of ATP.
source: We therefore conclude that Q203 and TB47 are bona fide analogs of the substrate, and thus ultimately function by hindering the downstream synthesis of ATP (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on structural and functional data.

claim: Q203 and TB47 are highly bactericidal against M. ulcerans, almost certainly targeting the Qp-binding site.
source: These two compounds are also highly bactericidal against M. ulcerans, almost certainly targeting the Qp-binding site (Liu et al., 2019; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019 and Scherr et al., 2018.

claim: The sequences of the QcrB subunits have high homology across pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: In summary, the sequences of the QcrB subunits have high homology across pathogenic mycobacteria (Lee et al., 2020b) and the essential residues (QcrBGlu313 and QcrBGlu314) that are involved in hydrogen-bonding interactions with the inhibitors (Pethe et al., 2013; Scherr et al., 2018) are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020b and sequence alignment data.

claim: The essential residues QcrBGlu313 and QcrBGlu314 that are involved in hydrogen-bonding interactions with the inhibitors are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: In summary, the sequences of the QcrB subunits have high homology across pathogenic mycobacteria (Lee et al., 2020b) and the essential residues (QcrBGlu313 and QcrBGlu314) that are involved in hydrogen-bonding interactions with the inhibitors (Pethe et al., 2013; Scherr et al., 2018) are conserved across pathogenic mycobacteria (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pethe et al., 2013 and Scherr et al., 2018, and sequence alignment data.

claim: The highly conserved residues involved in the binding of Q203 and TB47 suggest a consistent overall fold and binding site exists in mycobacteria.
source: The highly conserved residues that are involved in the binding of these two molecules in this region (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) suggest a consistent overall fold and binding site exists in mycobacteria.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence conservation data.

claim: Q203 and TB47 show antimycobacterial activity across many species.
source: This is also in agreement with the fact that Q203 and TB47 show antimycobacterial activity across many species (de Jager et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2019; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The structures of cytochrome bcc from M. tuberculosis and M. smegmatis have high similarity.
source: It is worth noting that the structures of cytochrome bcc from M. tuberculosis and M. smegmatis have high similarity (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), and no steric hindrance is observed between the Q203 and M. smegmatis cytochrome bcc (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: No steric hindrance is observed between Q203 and M. smegmatis cytochrome bcc.
source: It is worth noting that the structures of cytochrome bcc from M. tuberculosis and M. smegmatis have high similarity (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), and no steric hindrance is observed between the Q203 and M. smegmatis cytochrome bcc (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a structural observation.

claim: Q203 should have a similar binding mechanism and a similar effect on the activity of cytochrome bcc from M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis.
source: This observation indicates that Q203 should have a similar binding mechanism and a similar effect on the activity of cytochrome bcc from M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural similarity.

claim: The inference about Q203's similar binding mechanism is in good agreement with previous antimycobacterial activity data and inhibition data for the bcc complexes from M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis.
source: This is in good agreement with previous antimycobacterial activity data and inhibition data for the bcc complexes from M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis (Gong et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gong et al., 2018 and Lu et al., 2018.

claim: In other prokaryotic, eukaryotic and human Qp-binding pockets, many of the observed interactions with Q203 and TB47 would not be possible.
source: In contrast, in other prokaryotic, eukaryotic and human Qp-binding pockets, for example, from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Lange and Hunte, 2002), Rhodobacter sphaeroides (Esser et al., 2008), and human (Guo et al., 2017), many of the observed interactions would not be possible (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and citations.

claim: Q203 and TB47 should have low-binding affinity toward QcrB in non-mycobacterial bacteria and in eukaryotes.
source: This suggests that Q203 and TB47 should have low-binding affinity toward its counterpart QcrB in non-mycobacterial bacteria and in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural differences.

claim: Key residues that enable the binding of Q203 and TB47 in the mycobacteria are not present in other bacteria and eukaryotes.
source: Even if there is some flexibility in the Qp-binding pocket that enables some level of binding, key residues that enable the binding of Q203 and TB47 in the mycobacteria are not present in other bacteria and eukaryotes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data.

claim: The wild-type system has stronger affinity for Q203 than the mutant systems (Thr313Ala or Glu314Tyr).
source: It is suggested that the wild-type system has stronger affinity than the mutant systems (Thr313Ala or Glu314Tyr).
evidence: This is supported by binding free energy calculations.

claim: The binding affinity of Q203 in the dual mutant (Thr313Ala and Glu314Tyr) is significantly weaker compared to the wild-type or single-mutant systems.
source: The relative free energy of binding calculation for Q203 in the dual mutant (Thr313Ala and Glu314Tyr) indicates that its binding affinity is significantly weaker compared to the wild-type or single-mutant systems.
evidence: This is supported by binding free energy calculations.

claim: The observations correlate with the observed low general antibacterial activity and low cytotoxicity of Q203 and TB47.
source: In summary, these observations correlate with the observed low general antibacterial activity and low cytotoxicity of Q203 and TB47 (Liu et al., 2019; Lu et al., 2019; Pethe et al., 2013; Scherr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019, Lu et al., 2019, Pethe et al., 2013, and Scherr et al., 2018.

claim: These high-resolution structures will greatly accelerate efforts towards structure-guided drug discovery.
source: These high-resolution structures will greatly accelerate efforts towards structure-guided drug discovery.
evidence: This is a statement about the expected impact of the study.
